intro: Picture a small place decorated in warm brown teak, sitting inside Chiang Mai's old city walls, where you step out the door and find the moat, an old Lanna temple, and the walking street all within a short walk — Sri Chiang Yeun House is a family-run stay that many people choose for its location and its affordable price · It's a 3-star boutique house with 16 rooms, right by Chang Phuak Gate and Manee Nopparat Road, from about THB 700/night · This review pulls together real guest voices from several platforms and tells you the good and the things to watch for as they are — we didn't stay here ourselves.

body.html: Let's start with the big picture · Sri Chiang Yeun House is a small boutique-style stay in Chiang Mai's old-town area, inside the square city walls ringed by the moat · Its main selling point is very clear: location and price — you get to stay inside the old city walls, the heart of Chiang Mai, for a rate that starts in the high hundreds to low thousands of baht a night · The building is a small house decorated in warm-brown teak, with a Lanna feel mixed with simplicity · There are only around 16 rooms, which makes the atmosphere feel friendly and home-like rather than like a big hotel — the staff recognise guests and look after you in a family way · This isn't a luxury stay where you'd soak in the room all day; it's a budget base for people who plan to be out exploring the old town from morning till night.

So who is this place for · From real reviews, the people who love it most tend to be travellers who like exploring the old town, budget-minded couples, backpackers who want a clean private room at a good price, and people coming to Chiang Mai to make the rounds of temples, cafes and markets · If you plan to spend most of your time outside the room — visiting temples, sitting in cafes, walking the night market — and then just coming back to sleep, this place does that job well on a comfortable budget · But if you expect a hotel with a pool, a gym, spacious rooms, a soft luxury-hotel bed, or you want complete silence to really rest in the room — this might not be the answer, and you should consider other options that focus more on amenities.

The location and getting around deserve special praise · Sri Chiang Yeun House sits on Manee Nopparat Road in the Si Phum sub-district, right by Chang Phuak Gate, the city gate on the north side · It's just a few minutes' walk to the moat and the Chang Phuak Gate market, famous for khao soi, stewed pork leg and evening street food · Wat Chiang Man, the very first temple in Chiang Mai, is very close on foot · Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phra Singh, the highlights of the old town, are about 1-2 km away — an easy walk, or a few minutes by songthaew (red truck) or Grab · The Sunday Walking Street and the North Gate Jazz Co-Op, for live-music fans, are also within walking distance · Chiang Mai Airport (CNX) is only about 3-4 km away, roughly a 10-15 min drive · This place's location scores run high across several platforms, which fits the way many guests name it as the main reason they booked.
"Fantastic location — walk out of the place and you're at the moat, and you can visit several temples without taking a car. In the evening it's an easy walk to eat at the Chang Phuak Gate market."

Before getting into room details, let me paint the neighbourhood around the stay, because this is what you'll actually experience every day · The Chang Phuak Gate area is the northern corner of the old town — lively but not as hectic as the Tha Phae side · In the morning you'll see monks on their alms round, local coffee shops opening one by one, and people cycling around the moat · Midday is quiet and pleasant, good for wandering the old temples and ducking down lanes where wooden houses and tiny cafes are tucked away · Come evening the Chang Phuak Gate market buzzes with the smell of grilling pork and vendors calling out, turning into a food spot that even Chiang Mai locals come to · Getting to stay at a point where you can walk out into this kind of old-town life is value the room rate doesn't fully capture, and it's the reason many guests can accept the limitations elsewhere.

On the rooms and the decor · Rooms here are decorated mainly in teak, giving a warm Lanna tone, and many people praise the design as charming with a genuine Chiang Mai feel · There are several room types, from Deluxe Double and family rooms to a suite-style room · One thing to know is that most rooms are fairly compact, suited to a stay of a few nights rather than spacious · The key point that real reviews stress is to choose a Mountain View room at the back of the building, because rooms facing Manee Nopparat Road clearly hear traffic noise, since the place is right on a main road and the soundproofing isn't tight · The back rooms are quieter, and many have a mountain view or a better outlook · Some rooms have a small balcony where you can sit and sip a morning coffee.

To cover the amenities fully · This is a small boutique house, so it has no swimming pool and no in-house spa, which is normal for this type of stay and price range · What it does have is free Wi-Fi throughout, breakfast (included in some rates, charged extra in others — check when you book), a small garden and a terrace to relax in, a lounge/common area, plus help arranging tours, car rental and an airport transfer · Rooms have air-conditioning, a TV, a small fridge, and a private bathroom with a shower · There's parking (mostly on the street) · One thing some guests stumble on is the payment policy, which at certain times is mainly cash, so it's wise to have cash ready and ask clearly before you travel · As for a spa and Thai massage, this area has plenty of good massage shops within walking distance, so it's not an issue for anyone who wants to unwind.

On food and bars · There's a made-to-order breakfast here, and many guests say breakfast is fine, with a decent range for a small place · But the real strength of this location is that you barely need to rely on the on-site restaurant at all, because the surroundings are packed with food · The Chang Phuak Gate market in the evening has khao soi, stewed pork leg, noodles and loads of desserts, just a few minutes' walk away · The old town has dozens of lovely cafes, both specialty coffee and sweets · For live music and evening drinks, the North Gate Jazz Co-Op with its live jazz band is not far · Put simply, the stay doesn't need to have a bar or a big restaurant, because the whole area is already a place to eat and drink.

On service · This is where reviews lean fairly positive · Because it's a family-run stay, the staff and owner are often praised as friendly, happy to help, and good at giving advice on places to see, restaurants and getting around town · Check-in is smooth, with luggage storage, help calling a car, and help booking a Doi Suthep tour or trips around the city · It's this friendliness that makes many guests feel as warm as if they were staying at a relative's house rather than a hotel · That said, because the team is small, housekeeping and attention to detail can sometimes be less consistent than at a big chain hotel, which is the trade-off that comes with a small budget stay.

Now for the real, unfiltered reviews — both praise and gripes, so you get the full picture · Praise: the location inside the old city walls is excellent, with temples and markets on foot; the teak decor is pretty and charming; staff are friendly and helpful; the price is good value for the location; and breakfast is decent · Gripes: the most-mentioned issue is traffic noise, because it's right on a main road with poor soundproofing, so front rooms are loud; some reviews say the bed sags or the mattress is uncomfortable in some rooms; some items are old and due for an update; the rooms are fairly small; the showerhead is mounted too high; and cleanliness is sometimes inconsistent, with a few reviews finding dust or hair in the room · The mattress and the noise are the two points to weigh most heavily before you decide.

"I really wanted to love this place because the design is pretty and the location is great, but the street noise really is loud and the bed wasn't very comfortable. A room at the back would have been a lot better."

On price and value · Room rates here start at about THB 700/night in the regular season, up to around THB 1,500-2,000/night for a larger room or high season · Compared with a location inside the old city walls, where stays in this kind of spot usually price higher, it's good value for people who care more about the location and old-town atmosphere than luxury · The overall score here is around 6.7/10 from several hundred guest reviews, which paints a clear picture — a stay with an excellent location and a good price, but where room quality and quietness are points where you need to lower your expectations to match the price · Set your expectations right and it's good value; expect more than the price level and you may be disappointed.

Things to know before you book, summed up point by point for an easy decision · One, always choose a back/mountain-view room to avoid the street noise — this is the single most important tip from real reviews · Two, have cash ready and ask clearly about payment methods before you travel · Three, if you sleep lightly or are serious about your mattress, ask the property about the bed condition of the room you'll get, or consider packing earplugs · Four, there's no lift and it's a small building, so if you have lots of luggage or find stairs difficult, ask for a ground-floor room · Five, check whether the rate you book includes breakfast · Six, during festivals (Loy Krathong in November, New Year, Songkran) the old town gets crowded and stays fill up fast, so book ahead.

In case you'd like to picture what a trip staying here looks like, here's a short 2-night plan using the place as a base · Day one: check in in the afternoon, drop your bags, then walk out to visit Wat Chiang Man and wander the old town in the cooler light, stop at a cafe for coffee, and in the evening walk to the Chang Phuak Gate market for khao soi and stewed pork leg, capping the night with live jazz at the North Gate Jazz Co-Op · Day two: wake up for breakfast at the stay, then have reception help arrange a trip up Doi Suthep or a car rental to tour around the city, come back in the afternoon to walk Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phra Singh, and if it's a Sunday, do the walking street at length · Last day: pack up, leave your bags, stroll for souvenirs around the old town, then take a car to the airport that's only just over ten minutes away — you can see how the location makes everything connect with barely any travel time lost.

To wrap up · Sri Chiang Yeun House is a small teak boutique house that sells its location inside the old city walls and an accessible price above all · It's a great fit for travellers who want to wake up and walk to temples, sit in cafes and stroll markets without paying for transport, and who don't expect resort-level amenities · Its strengths are the location, the charm of the decor, and the friendly family-style service · The things you have to accept are the street noise, the mattress quality in some rooms, and the age of some items · If you pick a back room, set your expectations to match the price, and value being right in the middle of the old town — this is a worthwhile, memorable choice for a budget Chiang Mai trip · We always suggest comparing prices across several platforms and choosing a free-cancellation rate to start with.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Sri Chiang Yeun House Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Sri Chiang Yeun House in Chiang Mai · what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 138/5 Manee Nopparat Road, Si Phum sub-district, inside Chiang Mai's old city walls, next to Chang Phuak Gate · A 2-3 min walk to the Chang Phuak Gate market and the moat · Wat Chiang Man is very close, and Wat Chedi Luang/Wat Phra Singh are within 1-2 km · Chiang Mai Airport is about a 10-15 min drive away.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Sri Chiang Yeun House · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 700/night for a standard room, up to around THB 1,500-2,000/night for a family room or suite · There are Deluxe Double, mountain-view, family rooms and a suite · Prices depend on the season, so compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Sri Chiang Yeun House noisy · which room should I choose?
faq.a: It's right on a main road with poor soundproofing, so rooms facing the road hear traffic · Real reviews recommend asking for a back/mountain-view (Mountain View) room, which is much quieter, and packing earplugs if you sleep lightly.

faq.q: Does Sri Chiang Yeun House have a pool or breakfast?
faq.a: No swimming pool, as it's a small boutique house · There's a made-to-order breakfast (included in some rates, charged extra in others — check when you book) · There's free Wi-Fi, a small garden, a terrace, and help with arranging tours/car rental/airport transfer.

faq.q: How do you book and pay at Sri Chiang Yeun House?
faq.a: You can book through Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com · The thing to know is that at certain times the property takes payment mainly in cash, so have cash ready and ask clearly about payment methods before you travel · We suggest choosing a free-cancellation rate to start with if your plans aren't firm.

faq.q: Who is Sri Chiang Yeun House right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers who like exploring the old town, budget-minded couples, and people who plan to be out visiting temples, sitting in cafes and walking markets all day · It suits people who value the location and teak charm more than resort-style amenities, and who are ready to lower their expectations on quiet and the mattress to match the price.
